values: Absolute Vending Solutions - Premium Dallas Lead Pack
Built 2026-06-18. Ranked, source-backed, route-ready pilot list for the 10-lead Dallas vending/amenity brief.
Every row has public proof + route
Send one finished pilot, then convert rest to paid production
What changed from the basic list
Rows are not alphabetical or padded. Best first move is at the top.

I started with Absolute Vending Solutions and completed the 10-lead Dallas pilot as a ranked, source-backed lead pack.

Each row includes the account, fit score, exact public signal, best contact route, first outreach angle, and a guardrail for how to position it. I also parked high-traffic but slower accounts as alternates instead of padding the primary list.

If this quality bar works, I can continue the same structure across the remaining briefs.
Existing vending/F&B is treated as a routing insight, not ignored.
Each row has a practical first route: service manager, property manager, facilities, guest services, or CBRE/property contact.
The client can immediately see what to say and why the account is relevant.
Hotels, mall, gym, and exact-existing-solution accounts are alternates/watchlist instead of weakening the top 10.
Every claim is auditable without hiding behind vague research.

Best client move: send this as one complete proof artifact for Absolute Vending, not as a promise to complete all 190 unpaid. The list is intentionally selective: cleaner routes and stronger public trigger proof outrank glamorous accounts with slow procurement. If the client likes it, the next step is paid/approved production for the rest.

values: Fast-reading client view: rank, fit score, exact proof, first move, and positioning guardrail.
Official service page names Express Service & Customer Lounge; basic maintenance is usually completed in one hour or less, and waiting customers get lounge Wi-Fi and refreshments.
Customer lounge, service waiting flow, service-drive guests

This is the cleanest account in the set: direct waiting-room proof, service-department ownership, premium customer-experience expectations, and a clear reason to add or upgrade unattended refreshments.
Call service first, then send a short note referencing the Express Service lounge and asking whether a premium unattended snack/drink setup is worth benchmarking.

Saw Sewell Lexus highlights an Express Service customer lounge with Wi-Fi and refreshments for customers who wait. Would it be useful to benchmark a premium unattended snack/drink option for that lounge?
Do not pitch cheap vending. Frame as a premium customer-experience upgrade or refreshment service benchmark.
Berkshire Hathaway Automotive profile says the store has service capacity for up to 50 cars, room for 700+ cars, and an attractive lounge for service patrons.
Service lounge, high-throughput service department, sales/service customer traffic
The service operation is large enough that even a modest conversion of waiting customers can justify a refreshment solution. It has better volume than most dealerships.
Route to service leadership, not general sales. Lead with the 50-bay service facility and service-patron lounge.
Toyota of Dallas publicly describes a large 50-bay service facility and service-patron lounge. Would a low-staff refreshment option improve that waiting experience?
Do not claim they lack refreshments. The pitch is service-lounge improvement and convenience, not replacement without proof.
Official AMLI page shows resident lounges, a community bar area, sky lounge, conference room, fitness center, yoga room, outdoor dining, and direct property phone.
Resident lounge, sky lounge, coworking/conference areas, pool deck, outdoor dining
It has multiple common-area surfaces and a direct property route. A small smart cooler or micro-market can be positioned as resident convenience for work-from-home and after-hours use.
Call the leasing/property office and ask who handles resident amenity vendors.
Saw AMLI Fountain Place has resident lounges, a sky lounge, conference areas, and outdoor dining spaces. Would a stocked grab-and-go option help residents using those spaces after office hours?
Do not overstate buying intent. This is a strong amenity-surface fit, not evidence of an active vendor search.
Official amenities page lists sky lounge, co-working space, resident lounge, conference room, package management, fitness center, outdoor kitchen, and a coffee bar with Nitro Brew Tap.
Sky lounge, resident lounge, coworking, conference room, package area, coffee bar
It has unusually specific amenity proof plus a clean phone route. The smart angle is not generic vending; it is after-hours resident convenience around the lounge/coworking/coffee surfaces.
Call property office, confirm who owns resident amenity partnerships, then follow up with the amenity-specific opener.

The Langford lists coworking, a resident lounge, conference room, package management, and a coffee bar with nitro brew. Is there interest in a low-lift grab-and-go amenity for residents using those spaces outside staffed hours?
Because a coffee bar exists, pitch supplemental snacks/drinks or after-hours coverage, not a coffee replacement.
Visitor page lists guest amenities, free coffee, cable TV, Wi-Fi, visiting hours, cafe hours, grab-and-go items, and explicitly says 24/7 vending is available around the clock.
Visitor waiting, dining room vending, first-floor cafe, family/caregiver visits
This is not a cold guess; the site confirms the category already exists. The opportunity is upgrade, service takeover, or benchmarking current vending quality.
Do not ask if they want vending. Ask if they review vending service quality or vendor alternatives for the dining-room machines.

Your visitor page notes 24/7 vending near the dining room plus long visitor hours. If vending service quality or product mix is reviewed periodically, would it be worth comparing a modern unattended option?
Existing vending is a positive signal only if positioned as upgrade/takeover. Do not present it as an empty placement.

Official site describes a 457,000 sq ft Class A office environment, tenant services, conference center, bar/lounge, gourmet coffee, order-in lunch, team happy hour, 62,000 sq ft Life Time, visitor parking, and direct phone.
Tenant lounge, bar/lounge, conference center, visitor parking, office tenants, Life Time traffic

It has the office-camp amenity surface Absolute wants: tenants, guests, meetings, and a direct building phone. The right offer is supplemental convenience for tenants, not a standalone cafe replacement.
Call building management and ask who manages tenant amenity vendors for the lounge/conference-center area.
Premier Place highlights a tenant lounge, conference center, gourmet coffee and order-in lunch. Would a small unattended snack/drink option help tenants during meeting-heavy or after-hours windows?
Existing F&B means the pitch must be supplemental and low-friction, not competing with the bar/lounge.

Clubrooms, coworking, conference room, sky lounge, rooftop deck, fitness, package pickup

Start at the leasing office and ask who handles resident amenity partnerships.
MAA Cathedral Arts highlights clubrooms, coworking, a conference room, sky lounge, rooftop spaces, and 24-hour fitness. Would a stocked grab-and-go amenity be useful for residents using those spaces?
Do not pitch only as vending. Use resident amenity / convenience language.
Official building page describes a 58-story office tower, $70M renovation, outdoor plaza, tenant lounge, coffee/wine bar, fitness center, and direct CBRE contacts.
Tenant lounge, outdoor plaza, coffee/wine bar, fitness center, office tenants
Premium workplace account with unusually clear amenity proof and direct named contacts. It is high-value but likely more formal and slower than property-office leads.
Use the listed CBRE route and ask for the property management contact responsible for tenant amenity vendors.

Fountain Place highlights its tenant lounge, coffee/wine bar, fitness center and 1.7-acre plaza after a major renovation. Is there interest in a supplemental unattended refreshment option for tenant convenience?
Do not sound like a mass vendor blast. This account requires premium language and a property-management handoff.

Official visitor page lists hospital address/phone, visitor comfort language, valet parking, cafeteria hours, other dining options in lobbies, accessibility services, chapel, security, and visitor support resources.
Visitor lobbies, cafeteria gap windows, waiting areas, staff/visitor circulation
Heavy hospital traffic and clear visitor-convenience needs. It is worth including because the traffic is huge, but it should be treated as an enterprise account with a slower path.
Ask for the department managing visitor amenities or lobby/cafeteria vending, then send a tight follow-up.

Enterprise procurement risk is real. Do not rank this as the easiest close; rank it as high-value and slower.
